claims.text: High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution in lightweight HEAs.
Stabilizing a single-phase solid solution suppresses the formation of brittle intermetallic phases.
Controlled thermal and mechanical processing can produce a homogeneous, single-phase microstructure in the lightweight HEA.
A uniform single-phase microstructure resists grain-boundary segregation.
Entropy stabilization minimizes compositional fluctuations in the alloy.
Suppressing brittle intermetallic phases helps preserve mechanical strength and ductility.
Selective oxidation of particular alloying elements during high-temperature exposure forms a dense, adherent oxide layer.
The single-phase microstructure enables in situ formation of a protective oxide during thermal exposure.
A dense, adherent oxide layer contributes to structural integrity.
A dense, adherent oxide layer improves corrosion resistance.
Relative to the conventional lightweight-alloy baseline, the HEA will have at least 20% higher yield strength.
Relative to the conventional lightweight-alloy baseline, the HEA will exhibit enhanced ductility.
Relative to the conventional lightweight-alloy baseline, the HEA will exhibit a lower corrosion rate.
Relative to the conventional lightweight-alloy baseline, the HEA will form a thinner oxide scale after high-temperature exposure.
Relative to the conventional lightweight-alloy baseline, the HEA will form a more adherent oxide scale after high-temperature exposure.
At excessively high temperatures, protective oxide-scale formation may become impaired and the proposed mechanism may cease to hold.
In highly reducing environments, protective oxide-scale formation may become impaired and the proposed mechanism may cease to hold.
Mechanical loading beyond the elastic limit can cause microstructural degradation that invalidates the proposed mechanism.
